quote.text: There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all.
quote.author: Peter Drucker, management theorist (1963)

stories.kicker: Iran & the Gulf · From stand-off to tanker war
stories.headline: The Gulf tips into an open tanker exchange — and the first crack in the oil price is the demand side
stories.dek: A stand-off that had merely closed the strait became a shooting one this month: American strikes on Iranian tankers, an Iranian “exclusion zone,” and traffic through Hormuz down to a trickle. Then, with Brent above a hundred and seven, OPEC and the IEA both cut their demand forecasts — the bear case arriving before a single barrel is truly lost.

stories.kicker: The Big Picture · The hike into the shock
stories.headline: Warsh raises — and means it: the first rate rise since 2023, into an oil fire it cannot reach
stories.dek: A quarter-point, a unanimous vote, and a dot plot with sixteen of eighteen wanting more. The ten-year touched five per cent, the dollar had its best day since June, gold made records and bitcoin did not. The regime is higher-for-longer with a stagflation tail.

stories.kicker: Down the Rabbit Hole · The invitation
stories.headline: Radio-control rock crawling and bashing: two tempers, one obsession
stories.dek: One camp feathers the throttle to walk a scale truck over a boulder, inch by inch. The other launches it off a ramp at fifty and repairs what breaks. Both are the same hobby, and both are a deeper hole than they look.

stories.kicker: The island · The sky clears, on loan
stories.headline: The haze breaks on a gift of rain — and the exports climb, then slow
stories.dek: A day after the worst air in seven years, showers over Kalimantan did what a decade of law has not, dropping the readings back to moderate. August’s trade figures rose on an electronics recovery, but hard off a high base; and the ministry moved to shrink some classes.

stories.kicker: Buy It Once · Toothbrushes & oral-care tools
stories.headline: The one toothbrush feature worth paying for — and the three hundred dollars of theatre bolted around it
stories.dek: Judged from the mechanism up, the powered brush is a modest, real upgrade with exactly two features the evidence supports. Everything above them — the display, the app, the “smart” head that counts seconds — is the part you are sold, not the part that cleans.

stories.kicker: AI · The loophole under the launch noise
stories.headline: Five frontier models in ten days — and a side door that walks the chips through the wall
stories.dek: The headline was a wall of launches. The quieter story is a server subsidiary, outside the blacklist that names its parent, routing billions of dollars of advanced silicon into the exact market the export rules were drawn to seal off.

stories.kicker: Gear We’re Watching · The system on your head
stories.headline: Sonos puts the whole system on your head — if you already live in its walls
stories.dek: The Ace Ultra’s trick is to hop your music off a Sonos speaker and onto the headphones over Wi-Fi, and back again with a press. It is genuinely clever — and worth exactly nothing to anyone who does not already own the speakers.

stories.kicker: Objects & Escapes · Twenty seconds a year
stories.headline: Grand Seiko’s most accurate mainspring watch — and the clasp its owners begged for
stories.dek: The Evolution 9 Spring Drive Ultra Fine Accuracy reaches boutiques this month rated to twenty seconds a year, and fixes the one ergonomic complaint owners have made for a decade. It also asks a purist a pointed question about what precision is worth.

stories.kicker: Culture Desk · The widest split of the year
stories.headline: A witch sequel opens number one with a third from critics and ninety from the fans
stories.dek: Practical Magic 2 took the weekend on nostalgia and word of mouth, not reviews. The fifty-seven-point gap between what the critics scored and what the audience scored is the story — and a lesson in what a fan number actually measures.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · The ban, nine months on
stories.headline: The world’s first under-sixteen social-media ban barely moved the needle
stories.dek: Australia’s ban is the boldest thing any government has tried on children and screens. The first evaluation is in, and for a parent watching a twelve-year-old start secondary school it carries an uncomfortable lesson: the law changed the paperwork, not the behaviour — and it cost parents their line of sight.

stories.kicker: The Long Game · The vital sign on the footpath
stories.headline: Your walking pace out-predicts your cholesterol panel — and the trap in reading it
stories.dek: A large UK study asked whether five things you can measure without a blood test could beat blood pressure and cholesterol at predicting early death. Walking pace won. The finding is genuinely useful — and genuinely easy to over-read.

stories.headline: What’s worth booking — a Grand Prix with a Sprint, a sumo on sale Saturday, four nights in December
stories.dek: The bookable calendar, Singapore and the region, verified against promoters and venues. Three marquee picks: the Grand Prix, a full-group stadium return, and the Kyushu sumo whose tickets open in two days.

stories.headline: The collapse of the moat
stories.dek: For two centuries, distance was New Zealand’s cheapest drug policy — too far and too small to be worth a cartel’s logistics. That protection is gone, and “P” has settled not in the cities but in the small towns the economy left behind.
